Chapter Two: Finding and Owning Your True Passion
Before you can build anything that truly lasts, you've gotta figure out what lights you up inside. I’m not talking about following the latest trend, or copying what everyone else is doing. This is about digging deep and uncovering that subject, that activity, or maybe even a cause, that genuinely sparks your curiosity and fills you with energy.
So, how do you actually find this passion? Well, it starts with a bit of honest self-reflection, mixed with some real-world testing. Think about the activities that just naturally pull you in. What are those things you can talk about for hours, even if no one's really listening? Or those hobbies that fill up your weekends, the ones that never feel like work? Sometimes, your true passion is obvious. But other times, you’ve got to dig beneath the surface—ask yourself what really matters, and be honest about what actually brings you joy.
Owning your passion isn’t just about recognizing it. It’s about embracing it—fully—even if it feels a little unconventional, or you wonder if it’ll ever make money. Here’s the cool part: thanks to the internet, even the most specialized interests can connect you to a worldwide audience.
Let’s say you’re obsessed with vintage sneakers. Maybe you worry that’s just too niche, right? But by sharing your knowledge, your stories, and your reviews online, you’ll be surprised how many fellow sneakerheads, brands, and collectors are out there looking for exactly what you have to offer.
There are a few simple but powerful principles to keep in mind as you search for that core passion:
First, be honest with yourself. Pick something that feels real to you—not just something you think will sell.
Second, don’t chase the crowd. Trends come and go, but genuine interest sticks around.
Third, embrace what makes you unique. That unusual or super-specific passion might actually be your biggest strength online.
And finally, prepare for the long haul. Building something meaningful takes time, so choose a passion that you can see yourself loving for years—not just a few months.
Once you’ve zeroed in on what really drives you, the next step is to put yourself out there. Share your thoughts, your knowledge, and your experiences—even if it feels a bit scary at first. Whether it’s through blog posts, videos, podcasts, or just posting on social media, making your passion public is a powerful move. It shows you’re serious, and it invites others to connect with you.
Think about real-life examples you’ve probably seen. Maybe it’s a home cook who starts sharing recipes and kitchen tips online, or a fitness enthusiast who documents their training journey for everyone to see. Or maybe it’s a tech hobbyist reviewing the latest gadgets and breaking down new trends. In every case, that willingness to share, to be seen, and to engage with others—that’s what transforms a private interest into a true platform.
Here’s something to remember: finding and owning your passion isn’t a one-and-done thing. It evolves over time, shaped by feedback, by new discoveries, and by your own changing interests.
So, start with what feels most authentic. Commit to sharing it. And, above all, stay open to growth and change as you go.
